subject.title: fix(browser): keep CDP cursor text previews UTF-16 safe

question: Should browser cursor previews guarantee a fully well-formed decoded string before the value leaves page scope, even though CDP JSON transport succeeds and the existing Node stage already makes the consumed preview safe?
rationale: The branch proves a different intermediate JavaScript value but no transport failure or final-output defect, so accepting the extra page-side policy requires an explicit maintainability and invariant decision rather than a routine bug-fix judgment.

options.title: Keep the canonical Node cap
options.body: Do not merge the extra page-side helper unless a concrete CDP or downstream failure is demonstrated.

options.title: Adopt full page-side well-formedness
options.body: Require complete lone-surrogate sanitization and tests for malformed source text, not only a trailing high surrogate.

options.title: Narrow to boundary protection
options.body: Only prevent truncation from splitting a valid surrogate pair and remove claims that all returned text is well-formed.

recommendation.title: Keep the canonical Node cap
recommendation.body: Do not merge the extra page-side helper unless a concrete CDP or downstream failure is demonstrated.
